decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add ... bookmarks — each has a URL”; “bare domains like `github.com` get `https://` added.” Round 1 client: “enough for me to save ... bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review presentation records URL-based bookmark saving that conforms to the requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit ... bookmarks — each has a URL, title, description, and tags.” Round 1 client: “enough for me to ... edit ... bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The presented add and later edit flows expose title and description before and after saving; the separate lack of automatic metadata collection is classified under REF-BM-02.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker defines editable bookmark fields as “URL, title, description, and tags,” omitting the required note field. Round 1 client: “I’m happy with the app as delivered.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the presented edit model lacks markdown-note editing. The client gives general approval without identifying or correcting that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks.” Round 1 client: “enough for me to ... remove bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The recorded delete capability conforms to the reference item.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: each bookmark has “tags,” with tag assignment included in add/edit. Round 1 client says the app is enough to “organize” bookmarks.
decisions.note: The presented bookmark model and editing flow support assigning tags; no conflicting behavior is recorded.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Tag sidebar — click any tag to filter.” Round 1 client: “enough for me to ... organize, find ... bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Clicking a specific tag to filter its bookmarks is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limits search to “title, URL, description, and tags”; the presented bookmark fields also omit notes. Round 1 client: “enough for me to ... find ... bookmarks.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the stated search corpus excludes the required note field. The client approves search generally but does not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “title defaults to the URL if left blank,” and offers “auto-fetching page titles from URLs” and “favicons” only as possible next directions. Round 1 client: “I’m happy with the app as delivered.”
decisions.note: The current save flow is explicitly presented without automatic title/favicon collection and therefore cannot satisfy the required complete metadata collection. General approval does not express awareness of the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “favicons” as something that could be added next, establishing that the delivered bookmark presentation lacks them. Round 1 client: “I’m happy with the app as delivered.”
decisions.note: The readability-first list requirement includes a favicon per item. Its stated absence is accepted only through broad approval, not an explicit acceptance of the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists “import/export (browser bookmarks / JSON)” among directions the app could take “next.” Round 1 client responds that the delivered app is enough and requests none of them.
decisions.note: Import is explicitly future rather than delivered, so Netscape-format import is absent. The client does not state the reference expectation or explicitly accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists “import/export (browser bookmarks / JSON)” among directions the app could take “next.” Round 1 client: “I’m happy with the app as delivered.”
decisions.note: Export is explicitly future rather than delivered, so Netscape-format export is absent. Broad approval is not an accepted-divergence response.
